walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 2: Drama — a core area of IGCSE Literature in English.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: Drama brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 2: Drama.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
Pathetic fallacy is when an argument in a story is weak or sad.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
Attributing human emotions or qualities to nature or inanimate objects to reflect a character's feelings or scene's mood (e.g. angry storms during conflict).

mcqs.q: Why are genre conventions important when interpreting a text?
options: Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
They set reader expectations the text can fulfil or subvert; analysing how a text uses or breaks conventions reveals its meaning and significance.
Genre is just a label to help bookshops categorise novels.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
